data: Asteroid · Jupiter Trojan · L4 · D-type · Slow rotator

One of the slowest-rotating bodies of its size known — a 446-hour (18.6-day) rotation period, unusually long for a 35-km asteroid. The slow spin suggests a complex collisional or tidal history with another body, possibly a recent (in geologic terms) major event.
35-km D-type L4 Trojan asteroid with an unusually slow 446-hour rotation period — one of the slowest spinners known among bodies its size. Lucy encounter 2028-04-18.
Leucus is an unusually slow-rotating L4 Trojan (445-hour period) — Lucy flyby April 2028 will image its odd elongated shape up close.
A planet that almost was — the rocky remnants between Mars and Jupiter that Jupiter's gravity wouldn't let coalesce.
